result.title: Subsurface schematisation from sparse CPT data using the tabular foundation model TabPFN
result.summary: Subsurface schematisation supports geotechnical decisions but remains challenging because sparse site-investigation data leave substantial gaps in information about ground conditions. This study explores TabPFN, a foundation model pretrained on general synthetic tabular data, for this task. Using only grid coordinates and soil behaviour type index observations from sparse cone penetration tests (CPTs), we first reconstruct two-dimensional sections without geotechnical fine-tuning or predefined layer boundaries. We evaluate the approach on synthetic sections and at two field sites in the Netherlands, comparing it with SchemaGAN, a conditional generative adversarial network trained on synthetic geotechnical sections, and with reference interpolation methods. In the baseline comparisons, TabPFN achieved mean errors close to SchemaGAN's on synthetic sections and lower mean errors at both field sites. On synthetic sections, TabPFN's mean absolute error decreased at each tested increase in CPT count, and, under the baseline input setting, its pointwise prediction intervals had mean coverage close to nominal levels. Subsequent fine-tuning on the synthetic sections used to train SchemaGAN improved synthetic test accuracy but increased mean errors at both field sites. These findings indicate that general-purpose tabular foundation models offer a promising route for updating subsurface predictions from sparse and evolving site-investigation data without retraining.

AI.brief_summary: 该研究将表格基础模型 TabPFN 用于稀疏 CPT 数据的地下剖面重建：仅输入网格坐标与土体行为类型指标，在无岩土微调、无预设分层边界的情况下生成二维剖面，并与 SchemaGAN 及插值基线比较精度与预测区间覆盖率。
AI.relevance_reason: 与视觉推理无直接关系，但其「由稀疏、逐步增多的证据直接做情境内推断并给出近名义覆盖的预测区间、免重训更新」的做法，可能为 LVR 中信念状态更新、证据充分性与不确定性标定提供类比线索，可供核查。
